speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the pattern of your symptoms, can you tell me if these issues started suddenly or developed gradually over time? Also, do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, particularly affecting your eyes and limbs, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve_Stimulation and REQUEST TEST: Single_Fiber_Electromyography. Can you tell me if you experience any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Repetitive Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Single_Fiber_Electromyography: Not performed in current data; Patient reports no difficulty swallowing or breathing.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The clinical presentation of fluctuating weakness worsening with activity, ophthalmoparesis (double vision on gaze), and limb weakness is classic for this condition, making the previous suggestion of Tuberculosis incorrect.
